result: Exact rmcp-v3.1.4 source has no dedicated protocol-level version, generation, prior-state, If-Match, or conditional-update field for tasks/get, tasks/update, or tasks/cancel. GetTaskParams carries only request metadata plus task_id; UpdateTaskParams carries request metadata, task_id, and input_responses; CancelTaskParams carries request metadata plus task_id. Task exposes last_updated_at as observable metadata, GetTaskResult returns DetailedTask, and update/cancel return TaskAckResult rather than a conditional mutation result. The ServerHandler dispatcher validates Tasks capability and then forwards these params directly to get_task/update_task/cancel_task; it adds no historical precondition. RequestMetaObject preserves arbitrary extension keys, so an application may define a custom fencing token in _meta, but that is application-owned metadata rather than stock task CAS. The smallest application-owned seam is therefore: authenticated/bound custom _meta expected-generation or stable-operation token, validated before mutation, with an atomic persistent-store compare-and-update on task_id plus generation. This still does not by itself fence an external non-idempotent effect.
scope_guard: Conclusion is limited to exact rmcp-v3.1.4 typed task models and ServerHandler dispatch at the pinned release. It does not prove the MCP extension specification forbids future/custom metadata fields, does not prove custom ServerHandler implementations cannot add stronger semantics, and does not prove external-effect exactly-once behavior.
